conviction_note: The company's own Q2 numbers (June exit of 2,997 bottles a month, Q2 net revenue about $734 a bottle) say a Q3 at the ~$7.1M bar only needs the Q2 monthly slope to keep going, so the number leans slightly to a beat (print_vs_bar +3%). The stock reaction leans less: this name bought a 5% revenue beat with +71% q/q growth at only +2.4% in August; payer access was stuck at 16% of the contracted book for two quarters and nothing since says it moved; and the unused $75M ATM is a mechanical overnight risk. The findings sum to about -0.1 and the scaled number is +0.26 (p_up 52 x abs 6.5). Both are close to zero, which is the honest read.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $7.1M and EPS -$0.33. Three estimate sources agree: Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-05 ($7.1M, -$0.33, +16% q/q; https://finviz.com/news/417314/alpha-cognitions-zunvale-ramp-faces-a-payer-test-as-street-models-slower-growth), Chartmill ($7.181M, -$0.34; https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ACOG/estimates) and Intellectia ($7.13M, -$0.33; https://www.intellectia.ai/ai-earnings-calendar/ACOG-FY2026Q3-earning-forecast-2026-11-11). Yahoo shows $9.78M across 6 analysts, but that is labelled CAD and comes to about $7.0M in USD. The company gives no revenue guidance. Its only guide is FY2026 R&D plus SG&A of $50-54M, cut from $54-58M in August.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 323k shares with 2.8 days to cover as of 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/acog). That is about 1.5% of the 21.78M shares outstanding (10-Q). Equibles showed 211k shares and 1.0 day on 2026-09-11 (https://equibles.com/stocks/acog/shortinterest). The short is not crowded. There is no usable option chain: baseline status no_paired_strikes, so no implied move and no skew. Holders: Opaleye (10%+ owner) bought on the open market on 2026-10-01, 10-15, 10-16, 10-22 and 10-23 at $8.23-8.69 and now holds about 3.29M shares, about 15%. Manchester Management filed a new 13G on 2026-09-23 for 6.9% (event date 2026-07-14). Run-up is +3.2% over 5 days and +1.7% over 20. The stock is 9.7% below its 52-week high and 95.6% above its low. Earnings Whispers says shares are down 8.7% since the last report and sentiment fell from 35.1% to 1.2% bullish. Turnover is about 106k shares a day, roughly $0.9M.

findings.finding: Demand exiting Q2 was 2,997 bottles in June, against 8,294 for the whole quarter, which means April and May together were 5,297 (about 2,650 a month). Q2 net revenue was $6.09M, about $734 a bottle (Q1: $3.54M on 6,054 bottles, about $585). Three paths for Q3: June held flat gives about 8,990 bottles and about $6.6M, below the $7.1M bar; the Q2 slope of about +6% a month gives about 10,100 bottles and about $7.4M, about 4% above the bar; the bar itself needs about 9,700 bottles at Q2 pricing. Management said momentum continued into Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-13 amc): revenue $6.09M against a $4.3-5.8M consensus, +71% q/q, and the stock moved +2.4% (8.63 to 8.84). Q1 2026 (2026-05-14 amc): +6.0% (5.68 to 6.02). Q4 2025 (2026-03-26): -4.9%. Q3 2025 (2025-11-13): -3.1%, on a revenue beat. Q2 2025: -19.9%. Q1 2025: about +27%. Closes are from Yahoo daily bars. Recent beats have bought only small moves.
findings.why_not_priced: The Street models +16% q/q after a +71% quarter (Earnings Whispers preview). If consensus had extrapolated the June exit rate and the Q2 monthly slope, the bar would sit near $7.4M rather than $7.1M. Revenue per bottle moved from $585 to $734 in one quarter and receivables rose $1.24M in H1. A partial reversal of that pricing would erase the beat, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The Q2 call commentary (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/13/alpha-cognition-acog-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) says July scripts were strong, Q2 had no material stocking and gross-to-net should stay stable through year-end. Same management, different document. There is no third-party script series. The Earnings Whispers preview calls the bar beatable but cites the same company metrics.

findings.finding: Payer access has not moved, as far as anyone has said. The Q2 release says the contracted Part D book was 'consistent at approximately 16%' for a second quarter, with 'expansion expected to accelerate in 2H 2026'. On the call management called access slower than expected because of IRA pressure on plans. Of the 17 company releases from 2026-08-13 to 2026-11-11, none announces a formulary or coverage win.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior event. The access shortfall was disclosed in the August print and the stock still rose +2.4%. Since then the stock has drifted -8.7%, and Earnings Whispers ties that partly to the payer question.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down 8.7% since the last report and the preview names payers as the test. But management's guide of '2H acceleration' is still the official stance, and a third quarter at about 16% would breach it. If the market had fully priced a miss here, the stock would sit near its post-earnings low of $7.98 rather than $8.77. The size is left small because the call could just as easily announce a 2027 contract win, which would be upside.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-05 (https://finviz.com/news/417314/alpha-cognitions-zunvale-ramp-faces-a-payer-test-as-street-models-slower-growth) independently flags that another flat quarter would be a credibility problem. The payer status itself comes from the same company Q2 release that finding 1 uses.

findings.finding: Opaleye Management, a 10%+ owner, bought on the open market on five days after Q2: 19,050 shares at $8.69 on 2026-10-01; 22,657 at $8.43 and 14,283 at $8.23 on 10-15 and 10-16; 17,117 at $8.33 and 14,973 at $8.23 on 10-22 and 10-23. That takes it to about 3.29M shares, about 15% of 21.78M. Separately, Manchester Management disclosed 6.9% in a new 13G filed 2026-09-23.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Opaleye has filed Form 4 purchases steadily since at least May 2026 (filings 05-19 through 10-26), so the buying is continuous rather than a new signal before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s from a fund are rarely aggregated for a microcap with about $0.9M of daily turnover. A 15% holder adding in the $8.2-8.7 range supports the price into any dip, which damps the downside tail. It carries no information about the quarter, since a 10% fund holder would not have the Q3 numbers.
findings.independence: Separate filings back the same point: Opaleye's Form 4 for 10-15/16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1595855/000149315226047631/ownership.xml), Opaleye's Form 4 for 10-01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1595855/000149315226045511/ownership.xml) and Manchester's 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1169253/000091957426006448/primary_doc.xml).

findings.finding: An offering could follow the print. There is an effective $250M shelf (S-3 333-289792) with a $75M H.C. Wainwright ATM, unused through 2026-06-30. Cash was $41.4M at Q2. Of the $12.8M Q2 drop, $6.06M was a one-off Galantos royalty buyout, so the underlying burn was about $6.8M a quarter. The 10-Q says current cash suffices for 12 months, raises no going-concern flag, and says management 'will need to raise additional capital'. The company did a $35M overnight offering in September 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The September 2025 $35M offering at $6.25 was priced outside an earnings window, and its reaction was not measured here.
findings.why_not_priced: What the money would buy: the commercial ramp toward 2027 operating profitability. Bottles growing +37% q/q corroborate that ramp, so a raise funds visible demand rather than distress, and the sign is close to zero. What remains is the mechanical risk: a small-cap that raises the morning after a good print usually falls overnight. The probability of that inside this window is low.
findings.independence: The S-3 and ATM terms are in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655923/000121390025079892/ea0254070-s3_alpha.htm. EDGAR shows no S-3, 424B or 8-K financing filing from 2026-04-20 to 2026-11-11 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001655923.json).

findings.finding: CONVERGE topline was guided for Q3 2026 and came out on 2026-10-01, the first day of Q4. In 180-day cohorts, about 80% of ZUNVEYL patients reached a therapeutic dose against 37-54% on pooled generic AChEIs. The comparison is unadjusted. Dataset updates are guided for December 2026 and March 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the release day (2026-10-01) the stock went 9.00 to 8.70 (-3.3%), then 9.10 the next day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the release is six weeks old. It is filed so the panel can see that the main guided Q3 catalyst was delivered on time and is not a pending slip.
findings.independence: The Q2 release guided 'topline data for CONVERGE in Q3 2026' (https://www.alphacognition.com/_resources/news/nr-20260814.pdf).

findings.finding: On the automated Q2 call transcript, management is quoted saying a sublingual PK study would read out in Q3 2026. No such readout appears among company releases through 2026-11-11, so the call may disclose a slip or the data.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior sublingual disclosure event.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is small: management sizes it at 10-20% of patients and it is a 2027-plus product. The press release says only 'advance toward the clinic in 2027' and does not mention a Q3 PK readout. The transcript is automated and garbled in places, so the claim may be wrong, which is why the size is minimal.
findings.independence: The Q2 press release (https://www.alphacognition.com/_resources/news/nr-20260814.pdf) mentions no Q3 PK readout. That partly undercuts the transcript but does not contradict it.

findings.why_not_priced: It is small on a $7M revenue line, and the Earnings Whispers preview already mentions it as a modest tailwind.

baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to cut against. The modest beat lean agrees with the flat run-up (+1.7% over 20 days) and with a stock that has drifted 8.7% lower since August. That sentiment trough is mildly favourable for a beat, but the name's own record of small reactions to beats keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-lean finding went from +0.6 to +0.5, because the Q2 beat with +71% q/q growth bought only +2.4%.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the ATM/offering risk went from -0.5 to -0.2. The money would fund a ramp that bottle growth corroborates; there is no going-concern flag and the 10-Q states 12-month sufficiency.

Lesson 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number): the payer finding went from -0.8 to -0.7, because a coverage win announced on the call is equally plausible. The sublingual finding went from -0.2 to -0.1, because the press release does not repeat the transcript's Q3 readout claim.

Lessons 6 and 7 left the rest standing: three agreeing estimate sources make the bar solid, short interest is about 1.5% so there is no squeeze adjustment, and there is no skew. abs_move_pct and p_up are unchanged.
